ranked_hypotheses.summary: The checkout-svc v2.3.1 'Discount engine refactor' deploy at 10:02 UTC introduced a null-handling defect in PriceCalculator.applyDiscount. The NPE makes POST /checkout return 500. This includes the interaction case the Critic raised: v2.3.1 may now dereference a discount or price field from pricing-db that was always occasionally null. In that case the code change is still the trigger. Support: the deploy precedes the first NPE (10:04:51) and the first logged 500 (10:05:07). The NPE is in v2.3.1 code. A past incident matches this pattern (a discount null bug after a release, fixed by rollback). Gaps remain. The c1.1 re-query again returned only the 10:00 (0.4%) and 10:06 (23.5%) samples, so an onset between 10:00 and 10:02 is still not excluded. The earliest error evidence is the 10:04:51 NPE, which is after the deploy. There are also only three ERROR lines against a 23.5% error rate. Next step: get 1-minute error_rate_pct for 09:45-10:10 and diff applyDiscount null handling between v2.3.1 and the prior version. Then roll back and confirm the error rate returns to the ~0.4% baseline.

pricing-db, a direct checkout dependency, started returning null or missing discount or price records (for example after a data change or a schema migration done outside the deploy tool). applyDiscount then dereferences the null and throws an NPE. If this is the cause, a rollback alone may not restore baseline. c1.2 queried pricing-db, and every result came back empty: metrics, logs at all levels, and scoped deploys. Empty is not the same as healthy, because missing ingestion looks identical. Migrations made outside the deploy pipeline would not appear either. So h3 is neither confirmed nor refuted. Weighing against it: the NPE names v2.3.1 code, and a checkout-svc code change sits right before the first error. Next step: check pricing-db migration and DDL audit history, confirm pricing-db logs and metrics are being ingested, and inspect the discount rows involved in the failing requests.

Node CPU saturation, possibly from a noisy-neighbour batch job like the past incident, causes checkout requests to fail. CPU was 94% at 10:06, when errors were high. c1.1 confirmed that this is the only CPU sample, so there is no evidence on whether CPU rose before or after 10:02. Against this: every logged error is an application NPE, not a timeout or resource error, and the past noisy-neighbour incident caused latency, not 500s. Next step: pull 1-minute node_cpu_pct and request rate for 09:45-10:30, and check co-located workload scheduling.

The search-svc cache.ttl_seconds change from 300 to 60 at 09:58 UTC raised load on a shared component and indirectly broke checkout. This is unlikely. search-svc has no edge to checkout-svc or pricing-db in the returned graph, and the errors are discount-code NPEs, not cache or load failures. The missing dependency:inc01:0003 edge leaves a small chance of an unseen path.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back checkout-svc from v2.3.1 to the prior version and confirm checkout error rate returns to the roughly 0.4% baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: h1 is the highest-confidence hypothesis (0.75). The NPE is in v2.3.1 code, it follows the 10:02 deploy, and a past incident with the same pattern was fixed by rollback. Verify the error rate after rollback to confirm the fix.

recommended_actions.action: Pull 1-minute error_rate_pct for checkout-svc from 09:45 to 10:10 UTC to pin the error onset relative to the 10:02 deploy.
recommended_actions.rationale: The current samples (10:00 at 0.4% and 10:06 at 23.5%) do not exclude an onset between 10:00 and 10:02, and the earliest error evidence is the 10:04:51 NPE. A precise onset strengthens or weakens the deploy link.

recommended_actions.action: Diff applyDiscount null handling between v2.3.1 and the prior release, and check for any unguarded dereference of discount or price fields.
recommended_actions.rationale: Locating the specific code path that throws the NPE confirms the defect and identifies the field that is null, which tests whether the trigger is the code change or a null data value.

recommended_actions.action: Verify that pricing-db logs and metrics are being ingested for the incident window, since the empty results may reflect missing ingestion rather than health.
recommended_actions.rationale: h3 is currently neither confirmed nor refuted because all pricing-db queries came back empty. Confirming ingestion is required before pricing-db can be ruled out.

recommended_actions.action: Check pricing-db migration and DDL audit history for changes made outside the deploy pipeline around 09:45 to 10:05 UTC, and inspect the discount rows used by the failing requests for nulls.
recommended_actions.rationale: If pricing-db returned null or missing discount or price records, a rollback alone may not restore baseline. This check determines whether a data-side fix is also needed.

recommended_actions.action: Pull 1-minute node_cpu_pct and request rate for checkout nodes from 09:45 to 10:30 UTC, and review co-located batch workload scheduling.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only CPU sample (94% at 10:06) cannot show whether CPU rose before or after the deploy. Timing data is needed to test whether capacity contributed.

evidence_support.rationale: The core facts are all backed by the cited rows: the 10:02 v2.3.1 deploy (deploy:inc01:0001), the NPE logs (log:inc01:0003/0004/0006), the error-rate samples (metric:inc01:err:0001/0002) and the past null-bug incident (past:inc01:0002). Two citations are weak: h3 cites log:inc01:0003 as support for a pricing-db cause, and one fact oddly says the deploy is '2-5 minutes after' a window.

fact_assumption_separation.rationale: Facts are cleanly separated and each assumption has a basis and a verification step. However, the assumption list is heavily duplicated and partly stale or self-contradictory. One assumption says 'no error-log evidence has been collected' while the facts cite three error logs. Another says the dependency list 'is complete' while its own basis argues it may not be. Some items, such as the request_rate gap, are really facts.

recommended_actions.rationale: Rolling back v2.3.1 with verification against the ~0.4% baseline is the correct first move, backed by diffing applyDiscount and pinning the onset minute. The follow-up checks on pricing-db data and the CPU timeline are proportionate, low-risk and specific.

fell_for_trap.rationale: The CPU/noisy-neighbour story (metric:inc01:cpu:0001, past:inc01:0001) is ranked low at 0.08 and explicitly argued against because the errors are NPEs, not resource errors. The payments-svc TLS trap evidence (deploy:inc01:0002, log:inc01:0008) is never used to support a conclusion.
